title: Signature Launch Plan (U-CONTRACT v1)
description: The shared launch-plan contract for Skill 49 / Skill 83 launches. One plan lists every unit (pages, email sequences, text sets, automations, optional Conversation AI) with the units it waits for. Written by the launch planner (WF-LAUNCHERS), consumed by the runtime swarm (WF-SWARM), email lane (WF-EMAIL-A/B), text lane (WF-TEXT), automation lanes (WF-AUTO-A/B/C), AI lane (WF-AI) and Command Center (WF-CC). Changes after the first published draft are ADDITIVE only. Validated offline by shared-utils/signature_launch_contract/validate_launch_plan.py against the four fixtures in fixtures/. Nothing in a plan authorizes a send or a live switch-on: every email, text and automation is draft_only.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Bump only when a lane must change how it reads an existing field; additive fields keep this version.

launch_id.description: Stable slug for this launch, e.g. elevation-2026-11. Used as the progress-file and package key.

price_usd.description: Main offer price. The single source of every price a lane writes; never invent one.

payment_plans.description: true opens the failed_payment automation family (spec 3.3). false forbids it.

launch_calendar.description: Every deadline a lane writes comes from here. Truthful deadlines only (Skill 50 prover).

timezone.description: IANA zone for the calendar, e.g. America/New_York.

black_friday.description: Present only for Skill 83 Black Friday launches. Order law (calendar_law.py): teaser < countdown <= doors_open <= launch < cyber_monday <= last_call < doors_close.

a2p_ready.description: A2P 10DLC registration answered by the client. false keeps every text a draft and makes the package warn that texts cannot send until A2P is approved.

conversation_ai.description: Optional Skill 38 bot. requested=false means nothing is built and the package records 'Conversation AI: not requested'.

mode.description: none when not requested; otherwise the job the bot does when a contact replies.

commerce_units.description: Optional. Products, prices, order forms, bumps, one-click offers and payment providers a launch needs created or bound before sales open. Same unit-id and waits_for rules as every other unit.

approved_plan_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical plan the owner approved. Set only by the approval step, from the owner's own reply; a lane refuses an effect when the plan it holds no longer hashes to this value.

approval_ref.description: Reference to the Command Center approval record that minted approved_plan_hash. A named reference, never a credential.

asset_map.description: Shared-semantics boundary: BRAND/ASSET (BFL-000). What was chosen, what was actually produced, whether it is hosted, and the real URL when one exists. Optional; absent means nothing is recorded yet and no lane may claim an asset or a link. Never a placeholder: an unknown value stays absent or null.

brand_choices.description: The selected brand choices the client actually confirmed (palette role assignments, fonts, logo).

brand_file.description: Path or ref of the brand file the choices came from.

palette_status.description: provided, client-confirmed or suggested. A suggested palette is never paid for.

assets.description: One entry per final asset the launch produced.

page_id.description: The page unit id this asset belongs to, when it belongs to one.

final_identity.description: The actual final bytes. Identity is a hash, never a filename alone.

production_state.description: draft is a layout proof; approved means the client's recorded approval bound this exact hash.

url.description: The real hosted URL, or null. Never synthesized.

publication.description: Shared-semantics boundary: PUBLICATION (BFL-000). The existing authorization, the actual capability, the save/publish result and the observed status or URL. A save is never publication and a request file is never a review. Optional; absent means nothing was published.

authorization_ref.description: The already-existing authorization the publication ran under. Never minted here.

scope.description: The exact surfaces authorized for publication.

capability.description: Observed capability only. Never assumed from a module being present.

observed_status.description: The platform's own observed status, verbatim, or null.

resume.description: Shared-semantics boundary: RESUME (BFL-000). Where a stopped launch restarts from, proven by the run's own journal rather than by memory. Optional; absent means the launch does not claim to be resumable.

run_ref.description: The launch run folder the stages live in.

journal_ref.description: The durable journal/state file a resume reads. A raw launch-profile plan is refused; the journal is required.

resumable.description: True only when the journal proves the closed stages are still intact.

blocked_reason.description: Plain English: what is missing before a resume can continue.

unit_id.description: Unit identifier, unique across pages, email_sequences, text_sets and automations.

waits_for.description: Unit ids that must be COMPLETE before this unit starts. Empty means ready now. Must resolve to units in the same plan and must not form a cycle.

execution_stage.description: Shared-semantics boundary: EXECUTION STAGE (BFL-000). Which stage a unit or launch is in and the receipt that proves it. Optional; absent means no stage was recorded and no lane may report one complete.

stage.description: The stage name in the producing run's own vocabulary (Skill 71: image-inventory-prompts, image-generation-qc, image-map-upload, design-board, final-mockups).

receipt_status.description: The receipt's own status, in the vocabulary the producer actually writes: 71-blackceo-signature-page/scripts/stage_gate.py RECEIPT_STATUS and references/report-json.schema.json are pass, fail, blocked, not_authorized. Only closed + pass counts as a closed stage.

url.description: Approved page URL, or null while the page is only planned.

sections.description: Shared-semantics boundary: PAGE INSTALLATION (BFL-000). The page's own section/element identity and its full-width policy. Optional; absent means the page has no recorded section map yet.

full_width.description: The section's full-width policy as actually applied (create and edit alike), or null when not applied.

native_checkout_family.description: Shared-semantics boundary: PAGE INSTALLATION (BFL-000). The selected native checkout family. Never invented; null until a real family is chosen.

native_purchase_bindings.description: Shared-semantics boundary: PAGE INSTALLATION (BFL-000). Real native product/price bindings for this page. Empty means nothing is bound.

slot.description: The offer slot this binding serves, in the shared launch vocabulary: main, bump, upsell_1, downsell_1, upsell_2 (the offers slot enum in shared-utils/signature_launch/domain/launch.schema.json). order_bump is a commerce-unit kind, never a slot.

native_price_id.description: Null when prices are resolved by amount rather than a native price id.

installation.description: Shared-semantics boundary: PAGE INSTALLATION (BFL-000). The actual installation outcome, never a design-only claim.

readback_ref.description: The read-back that proves the page landed in the host.

promotional.description: Promotional sets are capped at 5 per launch (spec 3.2).

timezone.description: recipient_local unless the client asked otherwise.

template.description: Skill 44 template id to start from, or 'new' when the spec calls it 'new, small'.

build_rail.description: unknown until U-GHL-PROBE answers; automation lanes apply the answer when it arrives.

variant_tag.description: AUTOMATION VARIANT (BFL-000). The contact tag that marks WHICH purchased variant an automation serves (main / upsell-N / downsell-N). Declared once on the unit that installs the post-sale purchase handler and derived from the plan's own purchased slot (offer.packages[].slot), never a second variant identity. The launch-c reader carries it verbatim and the launch compiler binds it to the buildable template's variant placeholder; absent or null means the plan declares none and the helper must stay on its approved email sequence.

purchase_identity.description: AUTOMATION PURCHASE IDENTITY (BFL-000). The purchase-event identity the post-sale handler deduplicates on, as the native field the selected flow supplies. Only an event / transaction / purchased-line identity is sufficient; an order id alone groups several paid changes and is never a dedupe key. Absent means the plan declares none and the compiler records the identity as insufficient rather than guessing.

transaction_id.description: The native transaction field reference, e.g. ghl.transaction.id.

event_id.description: The native purchase-event field reference, e.g. ghl.event.id.

purchased_line_id.description: The native purchased-line field reference, e.g. ghl.purchased_line.id.

order_id.description: The native order field reference. Grouping only: an order id alone never deduplicates a purchase.

filters.description: Shared-semantics boundary: AUTOMATION (BFL-000). The intended trigger's filters, in the selected rail's own vocabulary. Optional; empty means the trigger has no filter.

actions.description: Shared-semantics boundary: AUTOMATION (BFL-000). The complete ordered actions the automation performs, including copy identity. Empty means the action list is not compiled yet; a plan with an empty list is never a complete automation.

copy_ref.description: The real body/copy this action sends, by reference. Null when the action sends nothing.

delay.description: The wait before this action, as the rail expresses it. Null when it runs immediately.

settings.description: Shared-semantics boundary: AUTOMATION (BFL-000). Workflow settings that change behaviour, chiefly reentry and enrolment.

reentry.description: unknown until the rail answers; never guessed.

enrollment.description: successive keeps a second purchase's fulfilment, deduplicated by the native event/transaction/line identity.

browser_work.description: Shared-semantics boundary: AUTOMATION (BFL-000). The browser steps the automation requires that the API cannot perform, so an operation owner can route them. Optional.

execution.description: Shared-semantics boundary: AUTOMATION (BFL-000). The actual execution result, recorded rather than assumed.
